seam.name: MoE activation rotation and q8_1 quantize at hidden width 4608
seam.baseline_kernel: fwht.cu fwht_cuda_block<512, 256, float, true>: the transform, scale and sign multiply copied verbatim, one block per (row, 512-block), one launch
seam.candidate_kernel: bf16 tensor-core matmul against the block Hadamard, block 512, nine blocks, fp32 accumulate: the prototype wmma kernel on the shared H_512 with the signs on the input (and on nine signed copies, and with the entries generated), and cuBLAS GemmStridedBatchedEx against the shared H_512
seam.note: the butterfly body is the one fwht_siglu_q8_cuda runs (moe-fuse.cu moe_fwht_block_transform is a copy of fwht.cu's block transform); the SiLU gate and the q8_1 write are common to both arms, so only the q8_1 write is timed

shape.rotation: normalized block Hadamard, block 512, signed per input element

basis.note: the true basis is one Sylvester H_512 (256 KB int8) shared by the nine blocks plus their sign vectors (4.5 KB); the per-block arms read nine signed copies (2.25 MB) and are kept as figures. The generated variant computes the entry from the indices and reads no basis

verdict.reason: at 23 rows the quickest tensor-core rotation costs 2.810 us against the butterfly's 1.265 us (cuBLAS GEMM alone 2.810 us, with the sign and bf16 pass 4.043 us; prototype on the shared basis 19.266 us; q8 chain 16.825 against 1.637); the basis read is not what loses (one pass over the 260.5 KB shared basis costs 1.072 us), a tuned tensor-core GEMM of the product does; the butterfly sits 0.193 us above the larger of a plain copy of the same bytes (0.892 us) and the shared basis read (1.072 us), the most any stored-basis rotation can save at this seam
